items.title: Nivolumab, Docetaxel, and Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies a combination of immunotherapy (nivolumab), chemotherapy (docetaxel), and hormone therapy for men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study focuses on patients whose tumors have DNA damage repair defects or show signs of inflammation. The trial is no longer enrolling new patients.

items.title: Lutetium-177-PSMA-617 Plus Standard Care for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares adding the radioactive drug Lu-177-PSMA-617 to standard hormone therapy versus standard therapy alone in men with metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. Over 1,100 patients have been enrolled across 20 countries. The study is no longer recruiting but continues to follow participants.

items.title: Saruparib Versus Alternative Hormone Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Sensitive Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether saruparib (AZD5305), a PARP inhibitor, combined with new hormone agents works better than hormone agents alone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. The primary goal is to delay disease progression on imaging. The study is no longer recruiting.

items.title: Lu-177-TLX591 Plus Standard Care for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluates Lu-177-TLX591, a radioactive drug targeting PSMA, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after androgen receptor pathway inhibitor treatment. The study is actively recruiting patients to determine if adding this therapy improves outcomes compared to standard care alone.

items.title: PDS01ADC With Docetaxel and Abiraterone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests PDS01ADC, an antibody-drug conjugate, combined with docetaxel and abiraterone in men with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, and with docetaxel alone in castration-resistant disease. The study aims to determine if these combinations are safe and effective. The trial is currently recruiting patients.

items.title: AAA817 After Lu-177-PSMA Therapy Failure in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2/3 trial tests AAA817 versus standard care in men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after Lu-177-PSMA therapy. Patients must have previously received hormone therapy and chemotherapy. The study is actively recruiting to see if AAA817 provides benefit after PSMA radioligand therapy fails.

items.title: Lutetium-177-Dotatate for Metastatic Prostate Cancer With Neuroendocrine Features
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies lutetium Lu-177-dotatate, a radioactive drug approved for neuroendocrine tumors, in men with metastatic prostate cancer that has neuroendocrine differentiation. The drug targets somatostatin receptors found on these cancer cells. The trial is recruiting to see if this treatment is effective for this specific type of prostate cancer.

items.title: Zanzalintinib for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Phase 2 Trial
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests zanzalintinib in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer, particularly those with soft tissue or visceral metastases who have progressed on prior treatment. The drug has shown promising activity in earlier studies. The trial is preparing to recruit patients and will run for up to 24 months.

items.title: Lu-177-Vipivotide Tetraxetan Versus Observation in Oligometastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares Lu-177-vipivotide tetraxetan (also called Pluvicto) to observation in men with oligometastatic prostate cancer that has progressed after initial definitive therapy. The goal is to control recurrent cancer and delay the need for hormone therapy while maintaining quality of life. The study is actively recruiting.

items.title: Opevesostat Versus Alternative Hormone Therapy in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares opevesostat (MK-5684) plus hormone replacement to switching to abiraterone or enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with one hormone agent. The study tests whether opevesostat delays disease progression better than switching hormone therapies. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Ac-225-FL-020 Radioligand Therapy for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates the safety, effectiveness, and pharmacokinetics of Ac-225-FL-020, a targeted alpha-particle radioligand therapy, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Alpha particles deliver highly potent radiation directly to cancer cells. The study is actively recruiting patients.

items.title: Ifinatamab Deruxtecan Phase 3 Trial for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests ifinatamab deruxtecan (I-DXd, MK-2400), an antibody-drug conjugate, compared to chemotherapy in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study aims to determine if patients receiving I-DXd live longer and have better progression-free survival than those receiving standard chemotherapy. Currently recruiting.

items.title: FG-3246 Antibody-Drug Conjugate for Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial evaluates FG-3246, a CD46-targeting antibody-drug conjugate, in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after one prior hormone therapy but have not received taxane chemotherapy in the metastatic setting. The study assesses safety, efficacy, and how the drug works in the body. Currently recruiting.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Treatment for Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig combined with abiraterone to investigator's choice of treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with chemotherapy-naïve metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival. The study is actively recruiting.

items.title: Dual BRD4 and AKT Inhibition Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed a new type of drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. These dual inhibitors overcome resistance caused by elevated c-MYC, a problem that limits the effectiveness of AKT inhibitors alone. Laboratory studies identified compound 21d as a promising candidate for further development.

items.title: Machine Learning Model Predicts Survival in Bone Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: Researchers developed a machine learning model to predict survival in prostate cancer patients with bone metastases who did not undergo surgery. The model analyzed data from over 3,000 patients and found that Gleason score was the most important survival factor, more important than clinical stage. This tool could help doctors identify high-risk patients who need aggressive early treatment.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Checkpoint Inhibitors in Metastatic Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This large analysis of 1,580 patients from 21 trials evaluated immune checkpoint inhibitors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer without biomarker selection. One-year survival was 63% and two-year survival was 39%. Combination therapy with checkpoint inhibitors plus other agents showed better outcomes than checkpoint inhibitors alone, though results were preliminary.

items.title: Zoledronic Acid Protects Bone Health During Enzalutamide Treatment for Prostate Cancer
items.summary: The BonEnza study found that metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients receiving enzalutamide plus hormone therapy experienced bone loss after 18 months. However, adding zoledronic acid (a bone-strengthening drug) prevented this bone density decline. This suggests men on these therapies should receive bone-protective treatment to reduce fracture risk.
